evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.4.4: nihil est quod tē moveat
terms.comment: With a genitive, “nothing (of)”: nihil novī, nothing new. “Nothing but” is nihil nisi or nihil aliud nisi (Cic. Amic. 20). “And nothing” is nec quicquam (see anything). Nihil nōn, “nothing not”, is everything (Lewis & Short).

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica et cōmica: Plaut., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.19: nīl habeō quod agam

phrases.latin: hoc igitur habēbis, novī nihil. quid ergō opus erat epistulā?
phrases.english: so there you have it: nothing new. Then why write a letter at all?

phrases.latin: jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis
phrases.english: for a long time now I haven’t known how you are, since you write nothing

phrases.latin: nīl habeō quod agam et nōn sum piger: ūsque sequar tē
phrases.english: I’ve nothing to do and I’m not lazy: I’ll follow you all the way
there is nothing to upset you

phrases.latin: est enim amīcitia nihil aliud nisi omnium dīvīnārum hūmānārumque rērum cum benevolentiā et cāritāte cōnsēnsiō
phrases.english: for friendship is nothing but agreement in all things divine and human, with goodwill and affection
